correctness.rationale: The equilibrium is p=1-d. The linearized current term is d(S-I), since the reaction contributes +d and migration contributes -2d. Four exact roots of unity yield factors F_0,F_±,F_2; imaginary-axis equations give T_s and T_c, while the alternating mode crosses later. The comparison reduces to strictly convex h(t) with unique positive root; the characteristic derivative ω(ω-b)/|1-pτe^{-iωτ}|² and q_*<1/√2 exclude stability recovery after the first critical delay. Perturbative two-/three-site calculations give minimal weak-dispersal cycle size. verify.py tests mode matrices, residuals, derivative formula and crossing numerically; finite tests are not the continuum proof.

value.rationale: The initiating migration-loss population work left intermediate dispersal mode selection unresolved for general networks. The four-patch closed one-way circulation is a natural smallest configuration permitting a spatially rotating onset under weak migration, and its exact unique switch to synchronized instability supplies a complete structural phase diagram. This distinguishes topology-driven oscillatory onset from the familiar reversible-network homogeneous onset without requiring a general network theorem. The crossing is a natural phase boundary, not a small incremental numerical gain.
